item.text: {"chapter_id":"7B","shard_id":"7B-S02","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E010","BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0018-E002","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E010","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0018-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E008","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0026-E016","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0026-E018","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0027-R01-E005","BATCH-0027-R02-E006","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"answers":[{"question_id":"7B.1","answer":"The shard contains substantial adverse evidence of repeated misleading or false public representations, especially regarding security, corruption, surveillance, and accountability. Mexico Evalúa reported that AMLO claimed organized crime behaved well in the 2021 elections, denied or minimized allegations rather than answering them, and promoted an approach whose stated rationale lacked adequate evidence. ARTICLE 19 and CPJ documented presidential stigmatization of journalists and denials of Pegasus evidence. Freedom House reported that the presidential 'Who's Who in Lies' segment was accused of presenting false or misleading claims, while AP reported statements contradicted by officials and crime figures. There is contrary or qualifying evidence that some claims are allegations or retrospective assessments, and that official or institutional cooperation occurred in some areas.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0018-E002","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0026-E016","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0029-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R01-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a comprehensive verified catalogue of statements, sworn testimony, or court findings.","Several adverse claims are based on investigative or advocacy reporting rather than final adjudication."]},{"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"The record is predominantly adverse on correction and remedy. Multiple sources report denials, attacks, or continued repetition after evidence emerged regarding Pegasus surveillance, Ayotzinapa, missing-person records, and corruption. The Ayotzinapa promise remained unresolved in 2023, with experts reporting withheld evidence and families alleging protection of the Army. The record also contains partial corrective or cooperative conduct: authorities supplied some information, CNDH recorded many partial or completed recommendation actions, and López Obrador complied with a Supreme Court order to appoint COFECE commissioners. These institutional responses do not establish personal correction by the ruler.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0021-R01-E008","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0029-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0026-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish a final judicial determination for every alleged falsehood or obstruction.","Many documented remedies concern agencies rather than a personal presidential admission or correction."]},{"question_id":"7B.4","answer":"The shard does not establish that López Obrador or close family personally profited from office. It does contain material evidence of corruption risks, alleged diversion at Segalmex, weak beneficial-ownership controls, costly and opaque military-managed projects, and protection of a longtime associate connected to the Segalmex scandal. The sources characterize selective protection and accountability failures, but do not provide a final finding of personal enrichment by López Obrador or his family.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0028-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No asset, tax, gift, ownership, contract, emolument, or court record in the shard proves personal or family benefit.","The Segalmex and military-business evidence concerns administration, associates, or public projects and cannot automatically be personalized."]},{"question_id":"7B.5","answer":"Evidence indicates a governing preference for loyalty and political alignment over professional competence, alongside delayed or incomplete appointments that weakened independent bodies. Nexos described a loyalist administrative model; ARTICLE 19, Freedom House, and the Supreme Court record documented appointment failures affecting COFECE, IFT, and INAI. Retrospective reporting also describes personal intervention in Morena's succession and recruitment of opposition governors. The record includes a counterexample: after a court order, López Obrador appointed COFECE commissioners.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0028-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0021-R01-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard is not a complete personnel audit and does not assess every appointee's qualifications.","Some claims concern the broader movement or Senate rather than an individually attributable presidential appointment decision."]},{"question_id":"7B.6","answer":"The shard shows repeated weakening or obstruction of independent scrutiny, especially regarding military conduct, surveillance, Ayotzinapa, transparency bodies, and access to records. Evidence includes withheld military documents despite presidential orders, alleged interference with experts and prosecutors, non-transfer of historical archives, delayed appointments leaving oversight bodies without quorum, and attacks on journalists and critics. Countervailing evidence shows functioning courts, CNDH investigations, UN cooperation, some disclosure and institutional collaboration, and judicial invalidation of executive measures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E010","BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0018-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E008","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0026-E018","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0027-R01-E005","BATCH-0027-R02-E006","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0026-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Personal direction is not established for every institutional failure or military act.","Some evidence is inherited, concerns subnational actors, or reports allegations rather than final findings."]},{"question_id":"7B.7","answer":"The shard documents mixed but substantially adverse compliance with accountability processes. Presidential and administrative conduct is associated with denials, delayed appointments, non-disclosure of military records, alleged interference with Ayotzinapa investigations, continued attacks on critics, and support for weakening INAI and other oversight institutions. Positive evidence includes compliance with the COFECE appointment order, some cooperation with CNDH and UN mechanisms, court review of executive action, and partial implementation of CNDH recommendations. These positive actions do not resolve the broader obstruction concerns.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E017","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0018-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E008","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E015","BATCH-0026-E018","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0029-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not show a complete record of subpoenas, judgments, audits, pardons, or disclosure duties.","Several obstruction claims are attributed to advocacy organizations, affected families, or investigative reporting."]},{"question_id":"7B.8","answer":"Evidence indicates a mixed-to-adverse good-faith record. The shard documents unmet promises on Ayotzinapa justice, demilitarization, corruption, transparency, and limits on executive power. It also reports policy rationales that were weakly supported or followed by outcomes inconsistent with stated objectives, including social programs potentially serving clientelism and military transfers justified as anti-corruption despite transparency risks. Some formal commitments and institutional measures were implemented, including cooperation frameworks, anti-corruption reforms, and selected appointments after court intervention.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E010","BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E017","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Some evidence is retrospective and evaluates outcomes rather than proving intentional opportunism.","The shard does not provide a complete promise-by-promise legislative and implementation record."]},{"question_id":"7B.9","answer":"The shard contains material evidence of possible clientelism, favoritism, and privileged political access, but limited proof of direct personal financial benefit. Mexico Evalúa found that unconditional social transfers lacked transparent criminogenic criteria and could have served political clientelism. Nexos described selective protection of close collaborators, including continued defense of Ignacio Ovalle amid the Segalmex scandal, and reported political recruitment and personal management of Morena succession. Evidence on military-controlled projects raises risks of opaque privileged access and weak accountability, but does not itself prove favoritism in procurement or licensing.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0029-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard lacks a complete procurement, licensing, pardon, or access ledger.","The clientelism and selective-protection conclusions are partly analytical or alleged and are not uniformly supported by final legal findings."]},{"question_id":"7B.10","answer":"The shard presents a mixed but materially adverse ethical example. Positive elements include personal austerity imagery, social and institutional initiatives, cooperation with UN and CNDH mechanisms, and some judicially compelled or voluntary corrective action. Against this, the record documents attacks on journalists, repeated denials or misleading claims, alleged protection of the military and close associates, weakened oversight bodies, opaque military expansion, and persistent impunity. Multiple sources describe these practices as normalizing distrust, selective accountability, or institutionalized denial, while the evidence remains insufficient to attribute every national integrity failure personally to López Obrador.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E010","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E006","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0018-E002","BATCH-0018-E003","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0021-R01-E008","BATCH-0021-R02-E001","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E016","BATCH-0026-E019","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0027-R02-E006","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E006","BATCH-0029-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0021-R01-E009","BATCH-0021-R01-E010","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not establish a uniform personal causal nexus for all institutional or national corruption indicators.","Open-system visibility, retrospective synthesis, and advocacy-source perspectives may affect the apparent balance of evidence."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["The shard contains no direct score and should not be converted into one without comparative chapter-level calibration.","Several records concern 2022, inherited conditions, retrospective assessments, or allegations; target-period fit and attribution must be preserved.","Country-level corruption, impunity, violence, and institutional weakness should not be treated as personal dishonesty absent a ruler-specific nexus."]}
